To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mean and variance in prevalence of infection and probability of extinction of infection in the early real-time growth of the epidemic on a configuration model graph can be calculated in closed-form and depend on the first few moments of the degree distributions of the configuration model.

the mean and variance in number of infectious individuals and the probability of extinction in a Markovian SIS epidemic on a configuration model depend on the first three, and the first two, moments of the degree of the individuals, respectively.

(a) the real-time growth, extinction and variance of the SIR epidemic on configuration model networks is determined by the degree distribution of the population, (b) the real-time behaviour of SIR epidemic growth, extinction and the variance in infection prevalence is not determined by the number of infectious nodes, and (c) the real-time SIR epidemic behaviour on configuration model networks can be calculated using multitype branching processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the real-time behaviour of an infection spreading through the population.
the real-time behaviour of an SIR epidemic on a heterogeneous network, using an analytic approach which is numerically fast and accurate.
the early time behaviour of an SIR epidemic on a configuration model, and we have found analytic expressions for the real-time behaviour of this process that are accurate for all times.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the configuration model provides a useful approximation for the real-time growth of an SIR epidemic on a heterogeneous population, but that the variance in the number of infected individuals is sensitive to the third moment of the degree distribution.
this paper presents a very interesting and important analysis that provides a useful tool for studying the early time behaviour of SIR epidemics on networks.
our results are valid for all degree distributions, and are exact in the large population size limit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the early real-time growth, extinction and variance of infection in a heterogeneous population can be accurately predicted by using only the first few moments of the degree distributions.
the configuration model is a useful approximation to the early real-time epidemic growth and variance on heterogeneous networks.
the early-time behaviour of the configuration model SIR epidemic can be accurately and efficiently described by a branching process with the degree of each individual as its type.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single parameter (the variance in degree) can be used to predict the early time real-time behaviour of a heterogeneous population.
the early behaviour of the SIR epidemic is highly sensitive to the degree of the individual(s) that first become infected.

the degree distribution of a population is a crucial determinant of the real-time growth of an epidemic, the variance of the number infected, and the probability that the infection will die out before it has had time to become established.
